claims.text: The owner's Leanpub page lists ten books, most stopped between 60% and 95% complete: Hacking Portugal at 95%, last updated December 2016, SecDevOps Risk Workflow at 64%, Generation Z Developers at 60%.
claims.quote: Hacking Portugal at 95%, last updated in December 2016; SecDevOps Risk Workflow at 64%; Generation Z Developers at 60%

claims.text: In August, agents wrote three books in a day on graphs.sgit.ai, about 100,000 words, which the owner read printed on a long flight; two months later they are still at v0.3.0, v0.2.0 and v0.1.0, under review.
claims.quote: Two months later they are still at v0.3.0, v0.2.0 and v0.1.0, which on that shelf means "the book is still under review".

claims.text: The reason is the same every time: a book is one big batch, so when the first version exists every change is expensive, review piles on one person, and when energy moves to the next place of highest leverage the book stays behind.
claims.quote: A book is one big batch. When the first version exists, every change touches everything

claims.text: The articles work the other way: each starts from a voice memo, is researched and checked, gets figures and a graph, and is released and live the same day, finished, with nothing waiting on the next one.
claims.quote: Each one is finished: nothing waits on the next one.

claims.text: When the owner rambles on a topic another article already covers, the agent puts in the link and goes to the nugget, so the signal to noise is high and the next memo builds on what is published.
claims.quote: it puts in the link and goes to the nugget. The signal to noise is very high.

claims.text: Of the three graphs books, the one about how the books were made read much better; its release notes explain that it was written over 41 narrated releases and 38 verbatim briefs with a repository it could question.
claims.quote: that book was written over 41 narrated releases, 38 verbatim briefs and a repository it could question

claims.text: When an agent like Claude has many of the owner's voice memos and the working history to learn from, it writes material that is authentic and reads well; the articles are exactly that kind of source.
claims.quote: it writes material that is authentic and reads well. The articles on this site are exactly that kind of source.

claims.text: The hypothesis: a book is a curated, ordered set of finished articles plus the editorial thread that connects them, and the workflow that makes the articles can make the books.
claims.quote: A book becomes a curated, ordered set of finished articles, plus the editorial thread that connects them

claims.text: What is not known yet is the right number of articles for a book, and how much editing is left once the articles are in order; the first book will tell.
claims.quote: What we do not know yet is the right number, and how much editing is left once the articles are in order.

claims.text: Books matter beyond revenue: they are a way to learn, to reach people, to share what is known, and to find users and adopters for the technology; a book on a table at an event says something a website cannot.
claims.quote: A book on a table at an event says something a website cannot.

claims.text: Agents with a mandate: about 32 articles and 113,000 words on behaviour policies, hooks, the mandate stack and agentics, enough for one book, maybe two, and the one that gives the most credibility at an event.
claims.quote: About 32 articles and 113,000 words on behaviour policies, hooks, the mandate stack and agentics

value.unit: articles on agents with a mandate

claims.text: Graphs that mean something: about 12 articles and 54,000 words, plus a book already half made on graphs.sgit.ai.
claims.quote: About 12 articles and 54,000 words, from introducing fractal semantic graphs to the wire as a graph

claims.text: Hacking Portugal, again: only about 8 articles and 25,000 words plus the 2016 book, so it needed new articles first, one per talk given about Portugal, which are now written for 2010, 2016, 2024 and 2025.
claims.quote: This one needs new articles first: one per talk I have given about Portugal, slide by slide, with what still holds and what I got wrong.

claims.text: Web Summit is in Lisbon from 9 to 12 November, and a book launch in Portugal during it would be a good way to test the hypothesis.
claims.quote: a book launch in Portugal while I am at Web Summit would be a great way to test this.

claims.text: The plan as targets: map each book by 19 October, write the missing articles by 23 October, assemble a 6x9 PDF by 26 October, publish on Amazon KDP by 30 October, order author copies, and have copies at the event.
claims.quote: By 19 October: map each book. Chapters, the articles in each, and the gaps.

claims.text: Amazon KDP's help pages say review takes up to 72 hours, and for accounts without a previously published book publishing may take up to 6 days.
claims.quote: for accounts without a previously published book, publishing may take up to 6 days.

value.unit: days publishing may take for a first book

claims.text: KDP sells author copies at print cost, up to 999 an order; for an address in Portugal they come from Amazon.es, and a 200-page 6x9 book prints for about €3.15.
claims.quote: A 200-page 6×9 book prints for about €3.15.

claims.text: The graphs site already built a print-ready 6x9 PDF of its first edition, so the tooling exists.
claims.quote: The graphs site already built a print-ready 6×9 PDF of its first edition, so the tooling exists.

claims.text: The bigger idea is other people's books: the constraints and failures of a story almost never get captured, and for people like rUv, with 226 public repositories, or Simon Wardley, that can now be captured and made into books.
claims.quote: I think we can now capture that, make it easy to consume, and help make great books from it.

claims.text: The owner will not start with someone else's story: a better workflow comes first, and like the wires, several books made quickly will show which finds its readers.
claims.quote: I want a better workflow first, and I do not want someone else's story to be my first experiment.

claims.text: The hypothesis is untested; the first book is the test.
claims.quote: The hypothesis is untested. The first book is the test.

claims.text: The dates are targets; Amazon gives no delivery time for author copies.
claims.quote: The dates are targets. Amazon gives no delivery time for author copies.

claims.text: The article counts are approximate, counted by hand from titles and tags.
claims.quote: The article counts are approximate. Counted by hand from titles and tags.

claims.text: The flight notes are the owner's; the graphs site records a bunch of notes, not each one.
claims.quote: The graphs site records "a bunch of notes", not each one.

claims.text: The article was written from a voice memo of 16 October 2026 by the site's agent, with the plan and editorial responsibility the owner's, and the sources read the same day.
claims.quote: the plan and the editorial responsibility are mine.
